crime_highlights: Mr. Boffa retrieved the two shotguns which had been inside the bag and handed one to Mr. Stump
They both returned inside the residence, each carrying a shotgun.
Mr. Boffa had his shotgun raised and pointed at Mr. Baldwin
and then he shot Mr. Baldwin twice, killing him
rationale_highlights: He is an aboriginal person who had what could fairly be described as a horrendous childhood.
He probably suffers from FASD due to his mother's substance abuse during her pregnancy with him.
he remains an intergenerational survivor and embodiment of this legacy

The moral culpability of Mr. Stump, in carrying a shotgun into Mr. Baldwin's residence, and in effect peripherally aiding Mr. Boffa in the killing, is relatively low, as compared to other manslaughter cases.
there are significant mitigating factors here
note: Passage 21 is long; Gladue effect folded into general mitigation.

crime_highlights: she was attacked from behind by one of the unidentified males, who grabbed her by the neck and forced her to the ground
the W.s were brutalised and threatened at gunpoint
Ms. W.'s and J.W.'s hands were tightly tied with zap straps, the latter's by Mr. Lesko
threatening to kill them if they did not
The W.s repeatedly begged not to be killed
He also fired his gun twice close to Ms. W.'s head.
rationale_highlights: Mr. Westell agrees that the Gladue principles nonetheless apply in this case
the knowledge may have played a part in his self-assessment or self-worth and, indirectly, his life history
his upbringing may have been somewhat more difficult for him than he wished the Court to consider
I also take into account Mr. Lesko's Métis heritage and the effects it may have had for him, as well as other challenges he may have faced
note: Court only says it takes Métis heritage into account; no stated effect on sentence.

crime_highlights: Mr. Thomas's vehicle suddenly crossed the centreline, proceeded diagonally across the northbound lane at a relatively high rate of speed
onto the far shoulder where Kim and Tracy Ward were walking
Ms. Ward had died on impact.
The injuries she suffered are permanent and life changing.
Ms. Ward was in the hospital for a year receiving extensive medical treatment, including brain surgery
it is clear she is a shell of her former self
rationale_highlights: both it and the presentence report highlight the damaging and traumatic experience Mr. Thomas's family and community in general have experienced, again because of colonization and the residential school system
Mr. Thomas has extended family who reported extensive emotional and physical abuse related to these experiences resulting in severe intergenerational trauma.
I am persuaded a term of imprisonment, somewhat less than suggested by the Crown, will properly reflect these factors
note: Conclusion in para 75 is general, listing Gladue principles among factors.
